title: Homemade dishwasher tablets
subtitle: Pressed blocks of washing soda, citric acid, and Castile soap
excerpt: Homemade dishwasher tablets are pressed blocks of washing soda, bicarbonate of soda, citric acid, and liquid Castile soap, moulded in an ice-cube tray and dried overnight. One tablet per wash cycle replaces a commercial tablet for most household loads. Makes sixteen standard tablets from one batch.
sourceNotes: Washing soda (sodium carbonate) as the primary dishwasher alkaline builder: Natural Cleaning Solutions by Rachel Ogden (2012). Citric acid as a rinse-aid additive and limescale prevention agent: standard in commercial dishwasher formulas (Reckitt Benckiser technical product notes, 2018). Liquid Castile soap as a surfactant: Lisa Bronner technical notes on Castile soap uses, publicly available 2021. Salt addition to help tablets release from moulds.

recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the batch to fill a larger ice-cube tray. The tablets are ready as soon as they are fully dry and firm.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dry for at least 8 to 12 hours before removing from the tray and storing. Tablets that are removed too soon crumble.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Six months in an airtight container away from humidity. The tablets absorb moisture from the air and soften if left exposed, store sealed. Discard if tablets crumble to powder when handled.

glossaryTerms.definition: Sodium carbonate, a strongly alkaline cleaning agent used in laundry and dishwashing. Not the same as bicarbonate of soda (baking soda), which is milder. Washing soda dissolves grease and lifts food residue in hot water.

content.text: Homemade dishwasher tablets are pressed blocks of

, bicarbonate of soda, citric acid, and liquid Castile soap, moulded in a silicone ice-cube tray and dried overnight. One tablet per wash cycle cleans most household loads. Makes sixteen tablets from one batch.

Do not mix the citric acid and washing soda dry without adding the liquid immediately, the two react on contact with moisture. Mix the dry ingredients first, add the liquid ingredients all at once, and press into the mould quickly.

items.prepNote: the alkaline builder; not the same as bicarbonate of soda, do not substitute
additional mild alkaline; softens the washing soda's alkalinity slightly
prevents limescale deposits and acts as a rinse aid; add to the dry mix last, before the liquid
unfragranced; just enough to bind the dry mixture without over-activating the citric acid reaction
optional; helps the tablets release from the mould cleanly

content.text: Combine the washing soda, bicarbonate of soda, and salt in a bowl. Add the citric acid and mix through. Add the liquid Castile soap all at once and stir quickly, the mixture will fizz as the acid meets the alkaline ingredients. Work fast: press the mixture into the silicone ice-cube tray compartments immediately, packing firmly with a spatula or the back of a spoon. The mixture should just hold together when pressed; add one to two teaspoons more liquid if it's too crumbly to hold.
Leave the tray uncovered in a dry, well-ventilated place for eight to twelve hours. The tablets are ready when they are firm and dry to the touch and can be removed from the tray without crumbling.

Place one tablet in the dishwasher's detergent compartment. Add a separate rinse aid (white vinegar in the rinse-aid compartment works for most machines) if needed. These tablets work well at 60°C and above; results at 40°C vary by load.
Six months in an airtight container. Store away from steam and humidity, the tablets will soften and clump if left exposed.
